title: How CZ Became America’s Richest Inmate 🟡
alt_hooks: How did a former burger flipper build a $60B crypto empire from a prison cell?
He sold his apartment for $900k to buy Bitcoin. Then he built Binance.
From flipping burgers at McDonald's to the richest inmate in US history.

scenes.line: He became the richest inmate in American history while holding a multi-billion dollar empire.
Changpeng Zhao started from humble beginnings, working at McDonald's in Vancouver flipping burgers.
In 2013, a poker game changed everything when a friend introduced him to Bitcoin over drinks.
He went all in. He sold his apartment in Shanghai for $900,000 to buy entirely into Bitcoin.
Bitcoin crashed shortly after. But Zhao did not panic. He stayed focused on building infrastructure.
By July 2017, he launched Binance. It processed orders at lightning speed and completely dominated markets.
Within 180 days, Binance became the largest crypto exchange on Earth, handling billions daily.
Regulators closed in fast. US authorities investigated Binance for severe anti-money laundering failures.
In November 2023, CZ stepped down as CEO and pleaded guilty to federal compliance violations.
Binance agreed to pay a staggering $4,300,000,000 fine to the United States government.
In April 2024, a federal judge in Seattle sentenced CZ to 4 months inside a federal prison.
He served his time at Lompoc low-security facility in California, trading luxury for a tiny cell.
Despite sitting behind bars, his massive net worth remained completely intact due to his equity.
Released in late 2024, CZ remains barred from running Binance directly but keeps massive influence.
He became the richest inmate in American history while holding a multi-billion dollar empire.

description: The untold story of Changpeng Zhao, from selling his Shanghai apartment for Bitcoin to building Binance, paying a $4.3B fine, and becoming America's richest inmate.
pinned: Would you sell your house to buy Bitcoin like CZ did in 2013?
